findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the breadcrumb's drift gate with the outbound_fields suppression for parents whose ticket_type is None/empty: either emit a breadcrumb for that case too (matching what is actually suppressed) or explicitly state and justify why untyped-parent suppression is intentionally excluded from breadcrumbing.
evidence: outbound_fields.py:197 `parent_type = (local_ticket_types.get(local_parent_id) or "").lower()` then `if parent_type != "epic"` — a None/empty type IS suppressed
parent_breadcrumb.py:62 `if parent_type is None or str(parent_type).lower() == "epic": return None` — a None type yields NO breadcrumb

Plan Approach: 'On a bound child whose direct parent is type-collapsed (the suppression above)' — asserts the breadcrumb gate mirrors the suppression, but the two conditions diverge on None/empty parent type
findings.finding: The plan's drift trigger is described as mirroring the outbound_fields suppression ('parent is a non-epic'), but the suppression fires for a parent present in local_ticket_types with a None/empty type (parent_type = (get(...) or '').lower() != 'epic'), whereas the breadcrumb gate returns no breadcrumb when the parent type is None/absent. This leaves a class of type-collapsed children (parent present but untyped/empty type) suppressed outbound yet with NO breadcrumb — the exact under-defined-leaf case the plan set out to fix.
scenarios: A child whose parent is present in local_ticket_types but has an empty/unset ticket_type: outbound parent field is suppressed, but no breadcrumb is emitted, so the child stays an under-defined leaf with no pointer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency assumption for append-once (single-writer per child per pass, or note the accepted duplicate-under-race window) so the first-writer-wins claim is not overstated.
evidence: 'before appending, scan the resolved jira_comments ... for the tag; if present, emit nothing. This is append-once and stable across passes'
'first-writer-wins' assumes the first write is visible to the second scan, but a get_comments snapshot resolved earlier in a concurrent pass may not yet contain a just-posted breadcrumb
findings.finding: The append-once guarantee is a check-then-act (scan resolved jira_comments for the stable tag, then append if absent). Two concurrent reconcile passes over the same child could each scan before the other's breadcrumb is posted/visible, both find no tag, and both append — producing the conflicting duplicate the plan explicitly aims to avoid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a log/metric line when a breadcrumb is emitted vs. suppressed (already-present tag / no bound ancestor) so the new write path is observable.
evidence: Plan describes emitting an '{"action":"add",...}' mutation but the observability checklist item (metric/log/trace on new failure/emission points) is not addressed anywhere in the plan text.
findings.finding: The plan adds a new outbound write (a breadcrumb add_comment mutation) but does not specify any log/metric/trace when a breadcrumb is emitted (or skipped due to dedup, or skipped for no bound ancestor). Operators cannot observe whether breadcrumbs are firing or debug why one did not appear.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether the walk starts AT the type-collapsed direct parent (naming it when bound) or strictly ABOVE it, so the 'nearest represented ancestor' is unambiguous for a bound non-epic parent.
evidence: 'On a bound child whose direct parent is type-collapsed ... walk the chain upward and name the nearest ancestor with a bound Jira key (binding_store.get_jira_key)'
AC1: 'A bound child with a type-collapsed, bound parent appends exactly one breadcrumb naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key'
The suppression is type-based (parent_type != 'epic'), independent of whether that parent has a Jira binding, so a bound non-epic parent is both trigger and candidate.
findings.finding: The plan does not crisply define whether the type-collapsed direct parent, when it is itself bound to a Jira key, is the ancestor named in the breadcrumb or is skipped in favor of a higher ancestor. AC test_breadcrumb_emitted posits 'a type-collapsed, bound parent' and expects the 'nearest represented ancestor', but a bound-yet-type-collapsed direct parent is simultaneously the trigger AND a bound-key candidate.
findings.location: Approach ('walk the chain upward and name the nearest ancestor with a bound Jira key') vs AC test_breadcrumb_emitted
scenarios: Direct parent is a bound non-epic (has a Jira key but cannot be set as Jira parent): does the breadcrumb name the direct parent's key, or the grandparent's?
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence: 'The walk considers the type-collapsed direct parent itself as the first candidate — if it carries a bound Jira key it is the named ancestor; otherwise ascend.' (or the opposite, whichever is intended).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the new `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` dedup-tag convention as a named module-level constant with a comment (and/or a brief design note) explaining it is load-bearing for cross-pass append-once.
evidence: 'Dedup on a stable identity tag (<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->), not the variable ancestor key'
No mention of recording the new tag alongside RECONCILER_MARKER / _EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES or in a design/AGENTS note.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new stable, load-bearing marker convention `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` used for cross-pass append-once dedup, but does not capture this new marker/tag convention in any discoverable place (AGENTS.md / design note / alongside the existing marker constants).
scenarios: A future editor changes the breadcrumb body and inadvertently drops/alters the tag, breaking append-once idempotency silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the tag as a named constant near RECONCILER_MARKER in outbound_comments.py with a docstring noting it must remain stable for idempotent dedup.
